# Minimum Absolute Difference. Each pair is [smaller, larger], and the
# pairs are in increasing order of their first number.

@example Sorted, the numbers are -2, 1, 5, 9 and 12, with gaps 3, 4, 4 and 3; the two gaps of 3 give the pairs.
[9,-2,5,12,1]
=> [[-2,1],[9,12]]

@example The closest two numbers are 16 and 22, 6 apart.
[7,22,16]
=> [[16,22]]

@example With only two numbers there is one pair, however far apart they are.
[40,-3]
=> [[-3,40]]

# The two bounds: d is as large as it gets, 2 * 10^6.
[1000000,-1000000]
=> [[-1000000,1000000]]

# Three numbers spread wide: both gaps are 10^6.
[1000000,-1000000,0]
=> [[-1000000,0],[0,1000000]]

# Each bound next to a neighbour 1 away.
[999999,-1000000,1000000,-999999]
=> [[-1000000,-999999],[999999,1000000]]

# In decreasing order.
[50,40,31,20,11]
=> [[11,20],[31,40]]

# A progression: every gap is the smallest, and the middle numbers are in
# two pairs each.
[0,-3,6,3,-6,9]
=> [[-6,-3],[-3,0],[0,3],[3,6],[6,9]]

# Larger gaps tie first; the smallest gap comes last along the line.
[15,22,0,20,5,10]
=> [[20,22]]

# The smallest gap so far shrinks twice along the line.
[27,0,19,30,7,24,14]
=> [[24,27],[27,30]]

# The smallest gap at the start, in the middle and at the end.
[21,40,2,30,1,41,10,20]
=> [[1,2],[20,21],[40,41]]

# The closest two are the first and the last number of arr.
[100,3,50,77,25,101]
=> [[100,101]]

# A pair across zero.
[-50,100,2,-1]
=> [[-1,2]]
